newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria starts probe of illegal CD production.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria starts probe of illegal CD production.

text.p: Bulgaria, accused by western countries of abusing intellectual property rights, has launched a crackdown on firms making illegal compact discs (CDs), the interior ministry said on Friday.

The international music industry has urged Bulgaria to move against five CD plants which are estimated to supply about one in eight of the world's pirate CDs, destabilising the industry and costing it $100 million a year.

EU External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek, who visited Sofia earlier this week, urged tougher measures to protect intellectual property rights in view of Bulgaria's commitments as a member of the World Trade Organisation.
"Today the Interior Ministry launched the first raid, named Pirates, on the territory of the whole country in search of illegal production of compact discs," a ministry statement said.
Police swooped on CD producers in Sofia and in the towns of Botevgrad, Veliko Tarnovo and Stara Zagora, and inspected their production lines and stores, the statement said.

They confiscated some 2,000 CDs made by CHLS Holding and Unison CDM because they had no identification code, the statement said. Police plan to confiscate a further 6,000 CDs on suspicion of being produced illegally, it added.
Last November Bulgaria set up a system of identification codes which have to be engraved on Cds to identify the producer.
Intellectual piracy has flourished in Bulgaria since the fall of communism in 1989 led to the liberalisation of its markets.

The International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI), representing the $40 billion international recording industry, said Bulgaria was now second only to China in the export of pirate CDs, producing an estimated 15 million discs a year.
